record.notes: The price is the whole difficulty and the arithmetic decides the verdict. The page prints EUR 5.50 for the 1, 3 and 6 month terms, EUR 4.68 on 12 months and EUR 4.40 on 24 months, all marked 'for the first 24 months'. At the ECB rate EUR 4.40 = USD 4.92, which is under the line by 8 cents. But Contabo's own JSON-LD publishes a USD price for the same product of USD 6.60 against EUR 5.50, which implies a rate of 1.20 rather than 1.1193; at that rate EUR 4.40 = USD 5.28, over the line. So the row is under the line or over it depending on which of the vendor's two published conversions is used, and that is the caveat. The second caveat is the discount: 'for the first 24 months' means the EUR 4.40 is a first-term price, and the vendor's own checkout text says the contract 'automatically renews on a monthly basis at the standard prices' after the initial term, which is EUR 5.50 = USD 6.16 at the ECB rate. Worst case exposure is 6.16 / 4.92 = 1.25x. Third: whether a non-EU buyer pays the 'Including VAT' or 'Excluding VAT' figure is not settled here, because the card prints both against the same EUR 5.50.

extras.term: 24 months for the EUR 4.40 figure; 12 months at EUR 4.68
extras.price_arithmetic: EUR 4.40 a month on the 24-month term x 1.1193 (ECB reference, 2026-10-23) = USD 4.925, rounded USD 4.92. The 12-month term is EUR 4.68 = USD 5.24, over the line. The monthly term is EUR 5.50 = USD 6.16. Contabo's own JSON-LD implies EUR/USD 1.20 (USD 6.60 against EUR 5.50), at which the 24-month figure is USD 5.28 and over the line. It is a VPS, so no 730-hour multiplication.
extras.worst_case_note: 6.16 / 4.92 = 1.25x when the 24-month term ends and the plan falls back to the EUR 5.50 monthly standard price.

If EUR 4.40 is net, it is USD 4.92; if 19% VAT is added it is USD 5.86, over the line. So the VAT basis alone can flip this row

record.provider: Contabo Storage VPS — unlimited traffic, 300 GB–1.4 TB

free_tier.stated: Storage VPS 10: 300 GB SSD (150 GB NVMe option), 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM, €5.50/mo for the first 24 months. Top tier 1.4 TB SSD at €37/mo. Higher tiers listed as 'More storage available'.

egress.terms: Unmetered. Quoted verbatim: 'Unlimited Traffic* … Unlimited outgoing and unlimited inbound data transfer with 200 Mbit/s to 1 Gbit/s speeds. Fair usage policies apply.' This is the single most useful egress term in the slot: no byte meter, only a port-speed ceiling and a FUP.

record.tooling: Root KVM. SSH/SFTP/rsync/rclone. No object API.
record.chaining: No free tier. But 'unlimited traffic + capacity-priced' means the composition move is a single large instance rather than many free ones: 1.4 TB unmetered for €37/mo beats ten free tiers that all clamp.
record.limits_note: Network port is 200 Mbit/s on entry tiers under fair use policies. Setup fees apply on select billing terms.
record.reliability_note: Hostloc thread evidence: a user running Contabo at 3 TB says '现在用的contabo已经只剩1.4t了'. Capacity creep on a shared storage volume is the reported failure mode, not deletion. Widely used, oversold reputation.
